subject: Emergency Medicine
originalQuestion: Patient came with hemorrhagic shock, what is the first priority in management?
explanation: In hemorrhagic shock, the priority is control of the source of bleeding while simultaneously initiating resuscitation. Definitive hemorrhage control is critical to prevent ongoing blood loss.
title: Hemorrhagic Shock

subject: Rheumatology
originalQuestion: A 42 year-old female patient known having Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate weekly what drug should be used with it:
explanation: Methotrexate inhibits folate metabolism and can cause mucositis, cytopenias and hepatotoxicity. Folic acid supplementation reduces adverse effects while maintaining therapeutic efficacy.
title: Rheumatoid Arthritis / Methotrexate

subject: Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: A patient in hospital with MRSA cellulitis the best antibiotic to be initiated for the treatment is:
explanation: MRSA is resistant to standard anti-staphylococcal β-lactams such as flucloxacillin. Vancomycin is a standard treatment for serious hospitalized MRSA infection.
title: MRSA Cellulitis

subject: Pharmacology
originalQuestion: A woman taking oral contraceptive, which drug will interact with it:
explanation: Rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer and increases metabolism of estrogen/progestogen, reducing the effectiveness of combined hormonal contraceptives.
title: Oral Contraceptive Drug Interactions

subject: Immunology/Allergy
originalQuestion: A Female patient with pneumonia was injected with amoxicillin, then she developed dyspnea, hypotension and itching, what's the type of hypersensitivity responsible for this reaction?
explanation: Dyspnea, hypotension and itching immediately after a β-lactam strongly indicate anaphylaxis, which is a Type I IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity reaction.
title: Anaphylaxis

subject: Surgery/Trauma
originalQuestion: Patient had trauma and on abdominal examination, he had Cullen's sign, what is the cause here?
explanation: Cullen's sign is periumbilical ecchymosis caused by intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal bleeding. In a trauma patient, intra-abdominal hemorrhage is an important cause.
title: Cullen Sign

subject: Hematology
originalQuestion: A Female patient came to you with malaise, having fissures on the angles of her lips, on examination she had a painless mass in the right iliac fossa with unknown cause, what is the cause here?
explanation: Angular cheilitis can occur with iron deficiency. Iron deficiency may also cause fatigue, pallor, glossitis and other mucocutaneous manifestations.
title: Iron Deficiency

subject: Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: Which of the following causing mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis?
explanation: Leishmania braziliensis is classically associated with mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, particularly in South America.
title: Leishmaniasis

subject: Neurology
originalQuestion: Parkinson disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition, which is the neurotransmitter is responsible for this disease?
explanation: Parkinson disease is associated with degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, resulting in reduced dopamine in the striatum.
title: Parkinson Disease

subject: Infectious Diseases/Cardiology
lecture: Infective Endocarditis in IV Drug Use
originalQuestion: A GP got needle stick of patient who was an IV drug abuser, having infective endocarditis, what is the probable causative organism here?
explanation: S. aureus is the most common cause of infective endocarditis in intravenous drug users.
topic: Infective Endocarditis in IV Drug Use
title: Infective Endocarditis in IV Drug Use

subject: Respiratory/Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: What is the most common cause of Hospital-acquired pneumonia?
explanation: Among the options given, Staphylococcus aureus is the best answer. Hospital-acquired pneumonia is commonly caused by aerobic Gram-negative bacilli and S. aureus.
title: Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia

subject: Dermatology
originalQuestion: Which of the following drug is contraindicated in psoriasisis:
explanation: Systemic corticosteroids are generally avoided in psoriasis because withdrawal can precipitate severe rebound psoriasis, including generalized pustular psoriasis. Methotrexate, cyclosporine and acitretin are all established psoriasis treatments.
title: Psoriasis

subject: Obstetrics
originalQuestion: A pregnant female patient complaining of sudden onset abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding ,she is in 38 weeks ,her BP110/80 and there is lower abdominal tenderness ,her baby pulse rate 170bpm, the most important diagnosis:
explanation: Placental abruption typically presents with painful vaginal bleeding, abdominal/uterine tenderness and fetal distress. Placenta previa classically causes painless bleeding.
title: Placental Abruption

subject: Epidemiology
originalQuestion: Consultant wanted to find evidence about incidence of deep venous thrombosis, the most accurate study is:
explanation: Incidence means the occurrence of new cases over time. A cohort study can follow disease-free individuals and measure the incidence of DVT.
title: Incidence / Cohort Study

subject: Pediatrics/Dermatology
originalQuestion: A 5 year-old child patient with skin lesion not itchy,painless on his chest, no fever, and systematically well ,which of the following is most appropriate dignosis:
explanation: Molluscum contagiosum produces painless, usually non-itchy, pearly papules with central umbilication. The child is usually systemically well.
title: Molluscum Contagiosum

subject: Gastroenterology
originalQuestion: A young patient complaining of vomiting and fatigue for few days then has dark urine, the possible cause is:
explanation: Acute viral hepatitis can cause constitutional symptoms followed by jaundice and dark urine due to conjugated bilirubinuria.
title: Acute Viral Hepatitis

subject: Gastroenterology
originalQuestion: Terry's nails are found in patients with:
explanation: Terry's nails are characterized by whitening of most of the nail with a distal band and are classically associated with chronic liver disease, especially cirrhosis.
title: Terry Nails

subject: Pediatrics/Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: The most serious complication of measles is:
explanation: SSPE is a rare but devastating, progressive neurological complication occurring years after measles infection. It causes progressive cognitive and neurological deterioration and is usually fatal.
title: Measles Complications

subject: Neurology
originalQuestion: A male patient with stabbing pain in jaw and mouth for few seconds which increased during toothbrush, what is the best drug for treatment:
explanation: Brief, severe, electric-shock-like facial pain triggered by touching the face or brushing teeth is characteristic of trigeminal neuralgia. Carbamazepine is a classic first-line treatment.
title: Trigeminal Neuralgia

subject: Cardiology
originalQuestion: A 62 year-old male patient with heart rate 72bpm and BP 220/110 mmHg with radio-femoral delay, audible systolic murmer, and notching in ribs at MCL on chest X.ray what is the possible diagnosis?
explanation: Radio-femoral delay, severe hypertension and rib notching due to collateral circulation are classic findings of coarctation of the aorta.
title: Coarctation of Aorta

subject: Cardiology
originalQuestion: A Patient with severe central chest pain, which radiates to left shoulder and jaw, he is stable with BP 150/100mmHg and pulse rate 74 bpm, he took aspirin, what is the next drug he should take?
explanation: In the context of the options provided, diamorphine is used for severe persistent pain associated with suspected acute coronary syndrome. Aspirin has already been given.
title: Acute Coronary Syndrome

subject: Pediatrics/Gastroenterology
originalQuestion: A 3-year-old child with a history of diarrhea 6 times per day for 6 months, with visible vegetable matter in stools. The child is thriving well, and development is normal. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Toddler's diarrhea is a common cause of chronic loose stools in otherwise healthy children who have normal growth and development. Undigested food particles may be visible in stool.
title: Toddler’s Diarrhea

subject: Infectious Diseases/Gastroenterology
originalQuestion: An elderly patient with watery diarrhea 6 times a day was admitted to the hospital due to an infection exacerbation while on co-amoxiclav. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Recent antibiotic exposure, particularly broad-spectrum antibiotics such as co-amoxiclav, predisposes to C. difficile infection causing antibiotic-associated watery diarrhea.
title: C. difficile Infection

subject: Endocrinology/Emergency Medicine
originalQuestion: A case of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), what is the correct dose of insulin infusion?
explanation: Standard IV insulin infusion for DKA is commonly 0.1 units/kg/hour, with monitoring and adjustment according to glucose, ketones and metabolic response.
title: DKA

subject: Endocrinology/Anesthesia
originalQuestion: A type I diabetic patient is on 15 units of long-acting insulin at night and regular insulin three times at meals. The patient is preparing for an anesthetic operation and fasting from midnight. What should be done regarding insulin?

options.A: Omit insulin at night and morning
options.B: Give insulin at night but not in the morning

explanation: A patient with type 1 diabetes must not be left completely without insulin because of the risk of DKA. During surgery/fasting, insulin requirements need adjustment and often a variable-rate IV insulin regimen with glucose monitoring is used.
title: Perioperative Type 1 Diabetes

subject: Genetics
originalQuestion: An adult wanted to start a family and he has Hemorrhagic telangiectasia, what is the type of inheritance?
explanation: HHT is usually inherited as an autosomal dominant disorder. Variable expression and incomplete penetrance can occur.
title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia

subject: Genetics
originalQuestion: A grandfather is a carrier of cystic fibrosis. What is the risk for his grandson who is 5 year- old?
explanation: Assuming the grandfather is a carrier and the child's parent is his child, the carrier probability for that parent is 1/2. If the other parent is assumed not to be a carrier, the probability of passing the CF allele to the grandson is 1/4 if considering only transmission from a carrier parent. However, the exact pedigree is incompletely specified; 1:8 is the intended exam answer in the supplied model.
title: Cystic Fibrosis Inheritance

subject: Cardiology
originalQuestion: A patient with hypertension and radio-femoral delay, with rib notching seen on X-ray at the midclavicular line. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The combination of hypertension, radio-femoral delay and rib notching is highly characteristic of coarctation of the aorta.
title: Coarctation of Aorta

subject: Epidemiology
originalQuestion: Which of the following give the best description to study the new cases of papilloma virus infection in collage student?
explanation: The question asks about new cases. Incidence measures the number/rate of new cases occurring in a defined population during a specified period.
title: Incidence

subject: Gastroenterology/Surgery
originalQuestion: In a patient with acute cholecystitis, what is the most common radiological imaging for the case?
explanation: Ultrasound is the usual first-line imaging investigation for suspected acute cholecystitis and is particularly useful for detecting gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening and sonographic Murphy sign.
title: Acute Cholecystitis

subject: Ophthalmology/Emergency Medicine
originalQuestion: A patient comes to the GP with unilateral painful redness of the eye, with no discharge. What should the doctor do next?

options.A: Referral to ophthalmology emergency department for assessment

explanation: A painful unilateral red eye without discharge can represent serious ocular disease such as acute glaucoma, keratitis or uveitis. Steroid drops should not be given without appropriate ophthalmological assessment.
title: Painful Red Eye

subject: Occupational Medicine/Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: A GP doctor got needle stick injury while performing venous cannula to patient known of intravenous drug use, what is the frist thing to do?

options.D: Encourage bleeding from site needle of the stick injury

explanation: The incident should be immediately reported through the occupational exposure protocol so that risk assessment and appropriate HIV/HBV post-exposure management can be initiated promptly.
title: Needlestick Injury

subject: Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: Which of the following antituberculosis drugs requires visual monitoring?
explanation: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, resulting in reduced visual acuity and red-green color discrimination abnormalities. Baseline and appropriate follow-up visual assessment is therefore important.
title: Tuberculosis Treatment Monitoring

subject: Rheumatology
originalQuestion: What is the best test for diagnosing giant cell arteritis?
explanation: Temporal artery biopsy is the classic confirmatory diagnostic test for giant cell arteritis. Treatment with corticosteroids should not be unnecessarily delayed when clinical suspicion is high.
title: Giant Cell Arteritis

subject: Orthopedics
originalQuestion: A patient presents with finger deformity after trauma with inability to extend his finger. What should be done for the deformity?
explanation: Inability to actively extend the distal interphalangeal joint after trauma suggests a mallet finger. Most uncomplicated cases are treated initially with continuous extension splinting.
title: Mallet Finger

subject: Hematology
originalQuestion: Most conforming test for Pernicious anemia is:
explanation: Pernicious anemia causes vitamin B12 deficiency due to autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells and intrinsic-factor deficiency. Serum B12 demonstrates the deficiency, although anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies can help establish the specific cause.
title: Pernicious Anemia

subject: Nutrition/Hematology
originalQuestion: An old patient presents with gum bleeding and hypertrophy. Which nutritional deficiency could be the cause?
explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes defective collagen synthesis, leading to fragile capillaries, bleeding gums, gingival swelling and poor wound healing.
title: Vitamin C Deficiency

subject: Pediatrics/ENT
originalQuestion: A mother with deafness from age 12 and using a hearing aid wants to confirm if her new baby is deaf. Which test should be used?
explanation: Auditory brainstem response (ABR/BAER) is an objective test used for hearing assessment in newborns, especially when behavioral hearing testing is not possible.
title: Newborn Hearing Assessment

subject: Neurology/Surgery
originalQuestion: A patient had a carotid artery surgery, the he has difficulty speaking, and when protruding the tongue, it deviates toward the right side. Which nerve is affected?
explanation: The hypoglossal nerve supplies the tongue muscles. With a unilateral lower motor neuron lesion, the protruded tongue deviates toward the side of the lesion.
title: Hypoglossal Nerve Injury

subject: Gastroenterology/Oncology
originalQuestion: A patient complains of dysphagia and is diagnosed with middle esophageal cancer that has metastasized to the liver. What is the best method to improve dysphagia in this patient?
explanation: In advanced esophageal cancer with metastatic disease, an esophageal stent can provide rapid palliation of dysphagia and improve oral intake.
title: Palliative Esophageal Cancer

subject: Rheumatology/Nephrology
originalQuestion: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis, Which marker indicates activity of lupus nephritis?
explanation: Anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies correlate with SLE disease activity, particularly renal disease, and rising levels can be associated with lupus nephritis activity.
title: Lupus Nephritis Activity

subject: Pediatrics/Infectious Diseases
originalQuestion: A girl had a sore throat with slight fever, malaise, then she developed maculopapular and partially vesicular spots on the hands and feet, with oral ulcers, what's the most likely cause:
explanation: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease is classically caused by enteroviruses, especially Coxsackie A viruses. It causes oral ulcers and vesicular lesions on the hands and feet.
title: Hand Foot and Mouth Disease

subject: Infectious Diseases/Pulmonology
originalQuestion: A 62 year-old male patient with low immunity came with productive cough and dyspnea and CXR is showing chest infection, the indication of sputum examination is for:
explanation: In an immunocompromised patient with respiratory symptoms, particularly when TB is clinically suspected, sputum examination is important for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
title: Tuberculosis

subject: Urology
originalQuestion: A 22 year- old male patient complaining of swelling in left testis, can't be separated from the testis ,the it is firm and fluctuating, with bright trans illumination ,which of the following is true :
explanation: A hydrocele is a fluid collection around the testis and classically transilluminates. The description of bright transillumination strongly supports hydrocele.
title: Hydrocele

subject: Gastroenterology/Oncology
originalQuestion: Which is MOST SINGLE investigation aid in diagnosis of hepatocellular carcenoma:
explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a commonly used tumor marker in hepatocellular carcinoma. It is not sufficiently sensitive or specific to be used alone for diagnosis, but among the listed options it is clearly the best answer.
title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma

subject: Dermatology / Emergency Medicine
title: Dangerous Complication of Urticaria
originalQuestion: Patient came with urticaria, what's the most dangerous type?
correction: Angioedema is not technically a subtype of urticaria; airway angioedema is the dangerous complication represented by the option.
explanation: Angioedema involving the tongue, pharynx or larynx can cause life-threatening airway obstruction.
whyA: Dermatographism is generally a benign physical urticaria.
whyNotB: Contact urticaria may be allergic but is not necessarily the most dangerous option listed.
whyNotC: Cholinergic urticaria usually produces small wheals associated with heat, exercise or emotional stress.
whyNotD: Airway angioedema can rapidly compromise the airway.

subject: Pediatrics / Pharmacology
title: Co-trimoxazole Dose and Volume Calculation
originalQuestion: A 3 year-old girl patient in pediatrics department suffering from lower UTI, then the pediatrician ordered for her septrin about 2mg/kg, and her weight is about 12.5 kg, what is the required amount in ml of septrin "50mg/5ml" she will take every night?
correction: The mathematical calculation gives 2.5 mL if the prescribed 2 mg/kg refers to the component present at 50 mg/5 mL. Co-trimoxazole contains trimethoprim plus sulfamethoxazole, so the question should specify which component the dose refers to.
explanation: Dose = 2 mg/kg × 12.5 kg = 25 mg. Concentration = 50 mg/5 mL = 10 mg/mL. Volume = 25 mg ÷ 10 mg/mL = 2.5 mL.
whyNotB: 5 mL contains 50 mg, twice the calculated 25 mg dose.

subject: Respiratory Medicine / Critical Care
title: PaO2/FiO2 Ratio in ARDS
originalQuestion: Which is of the following about acute respiratory distress syndrome is correct?
explanation: ARDS causes severe impairment of oxygenation, resulting in a reduced PaO2/FiO2 ratio.
whyA: ARDS commonly causes tachypnea rather than a normal respiratory rate.
whyNotB: Pulmonary hypertension is not the defining diagnostic feature of ARDS.
whyNotC: Reduced PaO2/FiO2 is central to assessment of the severity of ARDS.

subject: Endocrinology
title: Pretibial Myxedema in Graves Disease
originalQuestion: Which of the following may be present in patient with hyperthyrodism:
explanation: Pretibial myxedema is an extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves disease and may occur in patients with hyperthyroidism.
whyA: Plethora is not the characteristic finding being tested here.
whyNotB: Pretibial myxedema is associated with Graves disease.
whyNotC: Pallor is not the characteristic finding associated with hyperthyroidism in this question.

subject: Dermatology
title: Initial Diagnosis of Tinea
originalQuestion: The best initial test to do in patient with Tinea infestation:
explanation: KOH preparation of a skin scraping is a simple initial investigation for suspected dermatophyte infection and can demonstrate fungal hyphae.
whyA: KOH preparation is a practical initial test for dermatophyte infection.
whyNotB: Wood lamp is useful for some dermatophytes but does not detect all fungal infections.
whyNotC: Biopsy is generally unnecessary for typical tinea and is reserved for atypical or uncertain lesions.
